title: One chaos experiment: inject latency for 1% of users, stop at the line, keep the finding
captions: First, measure normal. Checkout's p99 latency is about 300 ms. The hypothesis: if the ratings service gets slow, the 1 s timeout and the circuit breaker keep checkout's p99 under 1.5 s. The dashed line at 1.5 s is the stop line.
Add 3 seconds of delay to ratings calls, but only for 1% of users. They are the experiment group. Everyone else is the control group, so you can compare the two.

The experiment group's p99 climbs toward about 3.3 s and passes 1.5 s. The hypothesis is wrong. An alarm on that metric is the stop condition, so the tool ends the experiment without waiting for a person.
The delay is removed and the 1% group is back to normal within a minute. Only 1% of users saw slow pages, for a few minutes, while the team watched.

The finding: the ratings client used a 10 s default timeout, not the 1 s in the design doc, so a 3 s call never timed out and the breaker never opened. Fix the config, then run the same experiment again.
